sourceFacts.description: One left-hand frame K has origin O at the junction of positive X, Y and Z rays. X points right, Y up, and Z diagonally down-left. Labels K, O, X, Y and Z are present. The three shafts and their arrowheads are visible; no origin circle is separately required.

A second frame K1 has origin O1 to the right of O on the same horizontal baseline. X1 points right along that baseline; Y1 points up parallel to Y; Z1 points down-left parallel to Z. Labels K1, O1, X1, Y1 and Z1 are present with subscripts.

This is one combined diagram, not two panels. The X and X1 axis lines coincide with distinct rightward heads at different horizontal positions. O and O1 lie on this common line. The Y/Y1 and Z/Z1 pairs are displaced copies with identical directions. The perspective projection of Z is schematic, not a planar angle measurement.
A horizontal rightward arrow emerges from the Y1 shaft above O1, labelled vector v above it. It depicts motion of K1 relative to K, along positive X/X1.

A distinct black point above the common X line and right of O1 begins a horizontal rightward arrow labelled vector v1 above it. It represents the object's velocity in K1. The point's vertical offset is schematic separation, not a second motion axis or a measured coordinate.

Six axis shafts plus two velocity-arrow shafts, hence eight structural arrows. Separate over-letter vector accents are notation, not additional structural arrows. Two origins, two frame labels, six axis labels and two velocity labels. No lattice, ticks, lengths, numeric values, unit labels, caption inside this crop, or v2 arrow.

independentlyDerivedRequirements: Keep all six axes visible in one frame; preserve the common horizontal support of X and X1 and distinct heads.
Keep O1 to the right of O on the common X line and each Y/Z shaft attached to its corresponding origin.
Keep Y parallel to Y1 and Z parallel to Z1 with the source's upward and down-left positive directions.
Keep the frame-velocity arrow attached to Y1 and the object-velocity arrow attached to its own black point; both point in the positive X direction.
Retain O/O1, K/K1, X/X1, Y/Y1, Z/Z1 and vector v/vector v1 without label collision or origin ambiguity.
Do not add numeric speeds, dimensions, scales, a v2 answer arrow or velocity-addition formula inside the figure.

independentMathematicalAndUnitReasoning.frameDefinition: Edition text identifies v as K1 relative to K, v1 as object relative to K1, and v2 as the same object relative to K.
independentMathematicalAndUnitReasoning.units: v, v1, v2 and c all have velocity units. v1*v/c^2 is dimensionless, so the quotient has velocity units. The schematic contains no explicit units to translate or alter.
checks: For positive collinear directions, the two source arrows are rightward; no negative-direction convention is implied.
For v1 = c and a physical frame speed |v| < c, substitution gives v2 = c.
For v and v1 both small relative to c, the denominator tends to one and the result tends to v1 + v.
The diagram supplies frame relationships, not measured values from which an exercise answer is inferred.

modernAdditionsAllowedForClarity: Regularized shaft thickness and lengths, improved margins and spacing, semantic theme colors and readable typeset mathematical labels.
Subscript typography may replace handwritten subscripts; it must preserve identities.
Origin labels may be moved off their shafts without changing origin coordinates.
